text:
maya: quick note - observed a tail latency blip on host decode path during a traffic burst. investigating kernel selection + kvcache interplay.

maya: flame snapshot:
```
host-parse: +10%
grpc/writev: +11% small-write churn
kvcache: shard-7 eviction bloom (400ms window)
kernel: more fallback picks on batches < 6 sequences
```

hugo: did we change preparse buffer ownership recently? i recall a refactor that added temp copies for safety.

maya: yes, the serializer change introduced a safety copy for out-of-order frames. cheap normally but multiplies on tiny streams.

zack: immediate mitigation: 1) short-circuit safe-copy for in-order common case, 2) add coalescing write buffer at gRPC layer, 3) make eviction incremental.

ops-bot: mitigation patchset queued: https://git.internal/r/runtime/mitigate-tinystreams (includes safe-copy short-circuit + write coalesce) job=62071

maya: after canary with mitigations at 5% traffic, p95 dropped from 230->215ms. still seeing rare 320ms outliers tied to eviction storms.

hugo: long-term: instrument eviction to emit `evict_window_ms` and `evict_items` per-shard so we can detect synchronized spikes and tune soft thresholds.

zack: agreed. I'll also add a quick backpressure window on host-parse: if `small_write_count>4` then apply local coalescing and batch delay 1-2ms to reduce syscall pressure.

maya: good. opening TASK-1210 to track eviction metrics and TASK-1211 for coalesce/backpressure. will follow up with flame once 24h of steady rollout. cheers.
